findings.description: Every new case in 3059c2f goes red under a backout of the production edit it exercises, so none of them covers nothing; two side observations are worth recording, neither of which is a surviving case. Mutations were applied only in a cp -a copy at scratchpad/mut and the job branch was never edited (git status --porcelain empty at the end).
findings.evidence: Copy: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-k-arnett-repos-agent-guild/7188fa38-b39f-46d7-9b46-9e5e2fe93992/scratchpad/mut (cp -a of the working tree). Baseline restore: 53 passed, 0 failed. M1 (git checkout f32a490 -- codex-courier.py, the whole capture backed out) -> 47 passed, 6 failed, killing 'a retried crossing's ledger row carries attempts and one discarded entry', 'the discarded entry names the first attempt's own validation failure...', 'a blocked crossing still discloses the first attempt it discarded', both quota cases, and 'a single-attempt crossing carries attempts...'. M3 (drop `attempt_records[-1]["reason"] = malformed_reason`) -> 51 passed, 2 failed, observed 'reason': 'no failure reason recorded'. M5 (the constitution's own failing example: discarded entries carry the row's published duration_ms) -> 51 passed, 2 failed, 'discarded_duration=339 row_duration=339', killing the duration case. Observation 1: two further mutations survive, M2 (attempt_clock -> started_clock, row read: discarded duration 178 vs row 240) and M4 (per-attempt tokens read from post-fold usage_totals). Both are unreachable by construction rather than untested by choice: the loop is `for attempt in range(2)` (codex-courier.py:448) and only attempt 1 is ever discarded, so cumulative-through-attempt-1 is numerically the attempt's own figure and no fixture can distinguish them. Observation 2: the duration case is written `entry.get("duration_ms") != row.get("duration_ms")` with `entry = {}` when nothing was discarded (test_codex_courier.py:509-534), so it passes vacuously under M1; cases 1 and 2 run on the same fixture and do go red there, so the suite still catches that state. Observation 3: the 7cc2660 guard does not actually repair the mid-run abort. Under M6 (_append_ledger reverted to its pre-commit signature while the caller still passes six args, leaving stdout empty and `outcome` None) the suite dies identically with and without the guard, at test_codex_courier.py:393 `f"model={verdict.get('model')!r} identity={outcome['identity']!r}"` -> TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable, ten lines before the guarded line 403. The worker guarded exactly the dereference the task named; the earlier one the task did not name still aborts the run. None of M1-M5 produced a None outcome, so this mutation arm ran to completion honestly.

findings.description: Both commit messages say why the change exists and carry none of the enumerated tells, and the two commits are genuinely separate changes rather than one split for appearance; the guard commit's body does overclaim its own effect.
findings.evidence: `git log f32a490..HEAD --format='%B'`. Granularity: 7cc2660 is one line in one file plus its two generated copies (`git show 7cc2660 --stat`: 3 files, 3 insertions, 3 deletions, all the same edit `outcome.get("persisted")` -> `outcome and outcome.get("persisted")`), and it lands in the #142 model-echo block, which no part of 3059c2f touches; 3059c2f is the #116 capture and shares no hunk with it. Two causes, two commits. Tells: no headings added, no em dashes anywhere in the added lines (`git show 3059c2f | grep '^+' | grep -E '\u2014|\u2013'` empty), no inflated symbolism, no vague attribution, no negative parallelism. The one three-item run, 'The row's own tokens_in/tokens_out stay the cumulative sum, quota_event stays untouched, and an attempt the vendor reported no usage for writes null', is three genuinely distinct invariants and reads as neither padded nor trimmed. Overclaim: 7cc2660's body says 'Guard the check so a None outcome fails its own assertion instead of aborting the run', and a None outcome still aborts the run at test_codex_courier.py:393 (see the C-5 finding's M6 evidence). Minor, since C-10 judges the prose and the sentence is a claim about effect rather than a writing tell.

findings.description: Driven rather than read: a retried crossing's row carries attempts 2 and exactly one discarded entry whose reason names the first attempt's validation failure and whose duration is that attempt's own, the cumulative token totals are unmoved at 108/26, a quota abandonment keeps quota_event true with no discarded entry invented, an unreported per-attempt usage writes null rather than 0, and neither the stdout contract nor the persisted raw-attempts shape changed.
findings.evidence: Drove test_codex_courier.py's fake-CLI harness directly (loading only its helper prefix, so the suite's own asserts never ran). malformed_once row: {"attempts": 2, "discarded": [{"duration_ms": 318, "exit_code": 0, "reason": "codex output was not JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)", "tokens_in": 7, "tokens_out": 3}], "duration_ms": 386, "tokens_in": 108, "tokens_out": 26, "quota_event": false} -- 318 != 386, so the cumulative clock was not reused. quota_structural and quota_wording rows: {"attempts": 1, "quota_event": true} with no "discarded" key at all; codex-courier.py:494-499 passes None on that path. Fabricated-zero rule by reading plus exercise: `_usage([{'type':'turn.completed'}])` returns (None, None, None) (codex-courier.py:190-202) and `_discarded_entries` copies record['tokens_in'] straight through with no `or 0` (codex-courier.py:417-430), so a record with tokens_in None yields {'tokens_in': None, 'tokens_out': None}. Worker claim 1 re-derived independently: `git log f32a490..HEAD -- .agent-guild/scripts/_courier_lib.py` is empty and `git diff --stat` over the same path is empty, so ledger_record is untouched; the courier's stdout keys are ['attempts','diagnostic','identity','ledger','persisted','status','verdict'] with '_discarded' absent on all four modes driven; and state/log/courier-raw/T-054-sonnet-r0-codex.jsonl produced by HEAD diffs against the same file produced by the f32a490 courier in only the temp-dir and schema-path strings, with no new key. Worker claim 2, --attempts on every row including single-attempt ones: correct, not a defect. C-15's text carves out no exception, and the schema's optionality is what keeps the 21 archived rows valid (vendor-call.schema.json describes attempts as 'Optional and absent on every row written before #116'), which is a statement about rows already written, not a prohibition on new ones. ledger-append.py:314's help string 'omit for a single-attempt row' is guidance to callers rather than a contract, ledger-append.py only omits a key when the flag is absent (lines 272-275), and always writing it is strictly more informative: without it a reader cannot tell a one-attempt crossing from a pre-#116 row. No consumer reads the field -- the only other `attempts` in the tree is subagent-return.py:181-199, which validates the courier's returned outcome object, not a ledger line.
